findings.clause: §0C.17 (EC-4): "function FLOOR_EXEMPT(i: MintedIntent): boolean { return i.priority === 0 && (i.effect === 'NONE' || ...) ... }" and "function verificationFloor(i: MintedIntent, kind: WidgetKind): VerificationLevel { if (FLOOR_EXEMPT(i)) { ... return i.effect === 'HANDOFF' ? 'ANONYMOUS' : subjectFloor(subjectCapability(i)); } return maxLevel(EFFECT_FLOOR[i.effect], KIND_FLOOR[kind], subjectFloor(subjectCapability(i)), targetFloor(i.target)); }"
findings.conflictsWith: §0.16 S0.16 — "At Gate 5 the gateway recomputes `verificationFloor()` from the live tables and compares the session against **its own** result, never the stored one. **Any** difference between the stored and the recomputed floor — raised or lowered — refuses the submission with `SUPERSEDED / policy_floor_changed`"; §0.15 FR-4 and §0B.28 FR-4, which name `verificationFloor()` re-derived at `EP-INGRESS` Gate 5 as FR-4's one mechanism; §3.4 R3.4.2 and §3.9's Gate 5 row, which fix the comparand as the floor "stored in the `IntentRecord`". The conflicting declaration is §3.7's `IntentRecord`, which enumerates intent_token_hash, widget_id, tenant_id, principal_proof_hash, effect, capability, handoff_capability_ref, target, verification_floor, confirmation, input_schema_hash, requested_scope_hash, run_ref, approval_of_intent_ref, confirmation_of_draft_ref, the lifecycle timestamps, action_receipt_ref and the five conversation-content fields — plus §0.34's confirmation_of_ref/produced_by_intent_token_hash, §0C.26-ter's body_hash, EC-15's selection_domain and §0C.28-ter's c9_domain. **No `priority` member is declared on `IntentRecord` anywhere in the contract**; `priority` is declared only on `WidgetIntent` (§3.1). `role` is likewise absent from the record.
findings.consequence: `verificationFloor` is one function with one body (§0.13 "The sole derivation"), and Gate 5's only input is the `IntentRecord` plus the live tables. The two horns are both fatal and neither is addressed. HORN A — Gate 5 evaluates the amended function: it must read `i.priority`, an identifier no declaring shape carries, which is exactly the defect §0C.11-bis states as a rule and §0C.28-ter closed for `c9Capability`'s domain argument by adding `IntentRecord.c9_domain` ("A gate cannot pass an argument the record does not carry"). The mechanism FR-4 names is then not constructible. HORN B — Gate 5 evaluates the unamended maxLevel: the exempt result is by construction a proper subset of the max terms, so for three of the five FLOOR_EXEMPT intents the recomputed floor strictly exceeds the stored one on every submission, and S0.16's "any difference" refuses each with `SUPERSEDED / policy_floor_changed` and increments `widget_floor_divergence`. Worked: `reconnect_intent` (§2.6.15 SOURCE.3, HANDOFF class `s`) stores ANONYMOUS and recomputes `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED`; `editor_handoff_intent` (§2.6.16 SETTINGS.4, §2.6.17 FORM.4) stores ANONYMOUS and recomputes SESSION_VERIFIED identically; the `CONTROL`/`control.widget.dismiss` escape verb stores `CONTROL_FLOOR = ANONYMOUS` and recomputes `KIND_FLOOR[kind]`, which is SESSION_VERIFIED on CONSENT_STATE, IDENTITY_BINDING, PAYMENT_HANDOFF, APPROVAL and CLIENT_LIST — the same five kinds §0C.16 names. Because EC-4 also amends §4.5.4 step 1 to "A `FLOOR_EXEMPT` intent is never withheld at this step", these intents are now *delivered and rendered* and then refused at ingress: a live control that cannot act, which is strictly worse than the withholding EC-4 replaced. This falsifies, at `EP-INGRESS`, the outcomes four clauses assert: §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 ("below that floor it is the only interactive element retained"), §2.6.16 SETTINGS.4 / §2.6.17 FORM.4/FORM.6 ("survive EVERY step of the degradation ladder"), §0.25 and §3.12.6 (the escape verb "never dropped"), §4.7 V9 ("the escape verb is always live") and §4.8 A-5 ("The escape intent is always keyboard-reachable"). Fail-closed — it over-refuses and admits nothing, so it is not a security-contract violation — but it is an unsatisfiable conflict between same-precedence normative clauses. EC-4's own *Evaluation points* line (`EP-BUILD`, `EP-FIT`, `EP-MINT`) omits Gate 5 entirely, which is why the question was never asked.
findings.fix: Two edits, both in the shape the section already uses. (1) §3.7's `IntentRecord` gains `priority: number` (mint class D, `AUDIT_RETAINED` — an integer carrying no conversation content, so §0.52's reachability test stays green), added to **P-30**'s component list alongside `body_hash`, `selection_domain` and `c9_domain`, exactly as §0C.28-ter added `c9_domain` for the same reason. While there, promote `widget_kind` into §3.7's interface: it is required as `verificationFloor`'s second argument and as Gate 7's comparand, and today it is declared only in §2 K2, §2 K11 and §A1 P-02, never in the shape. (2) Widen the signature `verificationFloor` and `subjectCapability` are called with — they read only `effect`, `capability`, `handoff_capability_ref`, `target` and `priority` — to a named `FloorSubject` structural type satisfied by both `MintedIntent` and `IntentRecord`, so Gate 5 calls the same function rather than forking a second code path over a security-critical field (which §0.16 expressly forbids). Then add Gate 5 to EC-4's *Evaluation points* line and state that Gate 5 re-evaluates `FLOOR_EXEMPT` from the record, so the exempt derivation is the one compared on both sides and S0.16's any-divergence rule fires only on a genuine table change.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies (EC-18, item 2): "**K22's derivation is amended** to `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { refKey({k:'intent', id}) : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`, with the escape placed **last** in render order."
findings.conflictsWith: §4.8's `A11yBlock`, which declares `reading_order: InteractiveRef[]` — preserved verbatim by §0C.22-bis ("role_hint, label, description, reading_order, live_region — unchanged"); §0C.22-bis's `declare function refKey(ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveRefKey` where `type InteractiveRefKey = ${InteractiveRef['k']}:${string}` is a **string**; §0C.22-bis's totality rule `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order.map(refKey))`; and §0C.22-ter's A-2 predicate `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`.
findings.consequence: The amended derivation unions a set of `InteractiveRef` **objects** (left operand, `refs(interactive_paths(body))`) with a set of `InteractiveRefKey` **strings** (right operand, `refKey({k:'intent', id})`), and assigns the result to a member declared `InteractiveRef[]`. This is precisely the ref-versus-key confusion §0C.22-bis was written to eliminate ("`InteractiveRef` is an object type and cannot key a Record, so the key form is declared") and that §0C.11-bis eliminated for capabilities with `capKey`. Three consequences, all at `EP-MINT`: (i) the closed-shape validator refuses `reading_order` because its string members are not `InteractiveRef`s; (ii) `reading_order.map(refKey)` applied to a string yields `` `undefined:undefined` ``, so §0C.22-bis's set-equality rule requires `accessible_names` to carry a key no composer can mint — an assertion set that can never pass; (iii) `nameSourceOf(ref, env)` in A-2's predicate is handed a string, and `resolveInteractive(env, ref)` has no branch for it, so the function declared "total over InteractiveRef, never throws, never returns undefined" becomes partial on the very members EC-18 adds. Because §0.25 mints the escape on every envelope whose `input_lock !== 'none'` and on every body declaring `dismiss_intent` or `discard_intent`, this reaches BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, PAYMENT_HANDOFF, FORM and SETTINGS_DRAFT at minimum, plus the five kinds §0C.16 names. Fail-closed (the envelope is refused, nothing is admitted), but EC-18's stated purpose — "it makes an accessibility obligation the contract already states satisfiable" — is not achieved; as written it makes it unsatisfiable in a new way.
findings.fix: Strike `refKey` from the set-builder and let the union range over refs, matching the left operand and the declared member type: `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { {k:'intent', id: i.intent_ref} : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`, with deduplication defined on `refKey(ref)` (the injective key form) rather than on object identity — otherwise a `role: 'remedy'` intent already produced by an `interactive_paths` entry, as LIMITATION's `remedy_intents[]` are, is added twice and K22's set-equality rule fails for that kind. Say `id` is the `intent_ref` (§0.28: `{k:'intent'}` holds an `intent_ref`, never a token), and keep the "escape placed last" ordering clause unchanged.

findings.clause: §0C.22-quinquies: "`accessible_name_suffix: Partial<Record<InteractiveRef['k'], string>>; // '' is the default`" together with its populated row "| `APPROVAL` | `intent` | `audience_size`, `risk_tier`, reversibility — **the approve control** |" and "| `CLIENT_LIST` | `intent` | `audience_size` — **bulk intents only, never row refs** |".
findings.conflictsWith: §4.8.2's own APPROVAL row, which §0B.35 and EB-12 elevate to the normative per-kind artefact and expressly preserve ("its keyboard-model, text-alternative, live-region and non-colour-state columns stand"): "approve/reject are buttons; `audience_size`, `risk_tier` and reversibility appear in **the approve control's** accessible name"; §4.8.1 A-17 for CLIENT_LIST; and §0C.22's A-2 mechanism, "for every kind §4.8.2 names, equality with the row's composition applied to the emitted body".
findings.consequence: The declared type keys the suffix on **ref kind**, so its finest expressible scope is "every `{k:'intent'}` ref of this widget kind". Both populated rows scope their suffix more finely than that, in prose, and the two readings cannot both be satisfied. APPROVAL's `interactive_paths` are `approve_intent`, `reject_intent` and `detail_intent` — all `{k:'intent'}` — so the type reading forces the audience-and-risk suffix onto the reject control and onto the NAVIGATE `detail_intent`, while the row's own text and §4.8.2's text both confine it to the approve control; an implementer satisfies one clause only by violating the other, and A-2's CI check has no single answer for two of APPROVAL's three controls. CLIENT_LIST is the harder case and it is aggravated by EC-18: §0C.16 states that CLIENT_LIST carries the mandatory escape, EC-18 now places that escape into `reading_order` as an `{k:'intent'}` ref, and the type reading therefore requires the escape verb's accessible name to end in an `audience_size` — a member declared only per element of `bulk_intents[]`, with no referent for an escape. `nameSourceOf` supplies the prefix, but the suffix names content the body cannot produce, so the A-2 equality assertion for CLIENT_LIST cannot pass. Fail-closed at `EP-BUILD`; no authority is widened. The paragraph's own rationale — "It must be per-ref-kind because the scopes differ" — is correct and the retype fixed row-versus-intent; what it did not fix is intent-versus-intent, which is the granularity both populated rows actually need and which EC-18 made universal by adding escape and remedy intents to every kind's `reading_order`.
findings.fix: Key the suffix on the pair, not on the ref kind alone: `accessible_name_suffix: Partial<Record<`${InteractiveRef['k']}:${WidgetIntent['role']|'*'}`, string>>`, with `'*'` meaning every role of that ref kind and the more specific entry winning. Populate APPROVAL as `intent:primary` (the approve control) and CLIENT_LIST as `intent:primary` (the bulk intents), leaving `intent:escape` and `intent:remedy` on the declared empty default everywhere — which also discharges EC-18's added members without touching §4.8.2's four preserved columns. `SERVICE_SELECTOR`, `STAFF_SELECTOR` (`option:*`) and `ARTIFACT` (`intent:*`) are unaffected. Then restate A-2's CI check over the pair key, and extend the build assertion from "the column is present and non-`undefined` for all twenty-two rows" to "every populated entry names content the kind's leaf schema can produce", which is the assertion that would have caught CLIENT_LIST.

findings.conflictsWith: §4.1.1 L1 — "three minters, one key. A valid envelope can be produced only by (1) the C9 orchestrator's compose step, (2) a registered capability read endpoint, (3) the proactive scheduler for the canonical moments (§4.9)." §0C.28-quater names minter 1 ("run-bearing") and minter 2 ("the run-less registered-capability-read path") and does not name minter 3. §1.1.4's own gloss — "two paths mint envelopes: a coordination run and a registered capability read" — omits it identically. §4.9.1 PR1 expressly permits `REFINE` and `HANDOFF` on a proactive envelope, and §3.2's effect table requires a non-null `capability` on a REFINE and a non-null `handoff_capability_ref` on a HANDOFF, which §0B.7 fixes as C9 refs.
findings.consequence: On the proactive-scheduler path `correlation.run_id` is null (there is no run) and `correlation.agent_id` is null by construction (there is no registered agent) — for exactly the reason §0C.28-quater gives for the capability-read path, that §0.16 E-29's derivation "derived by the minter from the run's registered agent" has no input. Neither branch of the ruling covers that path, so the declaration's own IFF governs: `c9_domain` must be non-null for every C9-space intent, and nothing can derive it. Every proactive envelope carrying a REFINE or a HANDOFF is therefore refused at EP-MINT, and EC-11's second Gate 6 C9 branch has no `C9Domain` argument to pass for such an intent. This is the defect §0C.28-quater says it fixed ("The refusal as written would have made every C9 capability-read envelope unmintable"), reproduced one mint path over: a member declared with an IFF — a totality claim — that one of the three declared mint paths makes unsatisfiable. Fail-closed, but it silently removes the proactive surface §4.9 exists to specify.
findings.fix: Extend §0C.28-quater's blockquoted ruling to name minter 3 explicitly: "On the proactive-scheduler path (§4.1.1 L1 minter 3) `correlation.run_id` and `correlation.agent_id` are null by construction, `c9_domain` is `null`, and EC-11's second Gate 6 C9 branch reduces there exactly as it does on the capability-read path — the `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)]` row must exist, and the `c9Capability` domain half is not applied." Complete the truncated "Non-null IFF BOTH capability.space === 'C9'" to "Non-null IFF capability.space === 'C9' AND correlation.run_id !== null", so the member's declaration and its scoping agree.

findings.clause: §0C.28-bis EC-18(2): "K22's derivation is amended to `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { refKey({k:'intent', id}) : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`, with the escape placed last in render order."
findings.conflictsWith: EC-17, printed later in the same §0C.28-bis and carried in the same errata table §0C.13: "per-kind membership is exactly what `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths` produces — which is what K22's *mechanism* already says ('validateEnvelope recomputes the ref set from interactive_paths and refuses on any difference'). K22's rule survives verbatim; only its illustrative list is struck." §0C.13's EC-17 row repeats it: "K22's rule and mechanism stand verbatim."
findings.consequence: Two normative rulings of identical precedence, in the same subsection and the same errata table, that cannot both be satisfied by any envelope carrying an escape intent — i.e. every envelope with `lifecycle.input_lock !== 'none'` and every body declaring `dismiss_intent`/`discard_intent`: BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, PAYMENT_HANDOFF, FORM, SETTINGS_DRAFT, and by §0.27 CONSENT_STATE and IDENTITY_BINDING. Under EC-17's preserved mechanism, `validateEnvelope` recomputes the ref set from `interactive_paths` alone and refuses on any difference, so the escape ref EC-18 requires in `reading_order` makes the envelope unmintable. Under EC-18, its absence breaks §4.8 A-5, §0.25 and §0B.36's CONSENT_STATE and PAYMENT_HANDOFF rows, which all require the escape to be keyboard-reachable. This is an assertion set that can never pass, and it re-opens precisely the unsatisfiability EC-18 was written to close.
findings.fix: Amend EC-17's ruling and its §0C.13 row to scope "survives verbatim" to the enumeration EC-17 strikes, not to the derivation EC-18 widened: state that K22's mechanism recomputes `refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { the emitted escape and remedy intent refs }` and refuses on any difference. One sentence in EC-17, and one clause in its errata row.

findings.clause: §0C.28-bis EC-18(2), the same formula: "`reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { refKey({k:'intent', id}) : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`"
findings.conflictsWith: §4.8's `A11yBlock.reading_order: InteractiveRef[]`, which §0C.22-bis preserves unchanged ("…role_hint, label, description, reading_order, live_region — unchanged…"); §0C.22-bis's own key-form declaration "`InteractiveRef` is an object type and cannot key a Record, so the key form is declared" with `declare function refKey(ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveRefKey`; §0C.22-ter's `nameSourceOf(ref: InteractiveRef, env)`, declared "total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined"; and §0C.22-bis's validator rule `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order.map(refKey))`.
findings.consequence: The two operands of the union are differently typed: the left yields `InteractiveRef` objects, the right yields `InteractiveRefKey` template-literal strings, because `refKey` returns `${ref.k}:${string}`. Assigned to `reading_order: InteractiveRef[]` the union is ill-typed and no envelope can satisfy it. If it is built anyway, both declared consumers break on the escape and remedy entries: the validator rule applies `refKey` a second time, and A-2's check `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)` passes a string to `nameSourceOf`, whose switch on `ref.k` matches none of the seven cases — so the function declared total and non-throwing returns `undefined` and `.label` throws. This is the exact defect class §0C.22-bis introduced `refKey` to prevent, reproduced in the newest repair. Independently, the set comprehension binds `i` and then uses the free variable `id`, which nothing in the clause declares.
findings.fix: Write the right operand as `{ {k:'intent', id: i.intent_ref} : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }` — `InteractiveRef` objects, with the bound variable — and leave `refKey` to the `accessible_names` key computation alone, where §0C.22-bis already places it.

findings.clause: §0C.28-bis EC-18(2), closing sentence: "Both added roles are `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT`, so this widens no authority — it makes an accessibility obligation the contract already states satisfiable."
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.18: "The L11 extension remedy is deliberately NOT in this set, and the reason matters: it is a `REFINE` on the widget's own owner capability, so a principal below that capability's floor could not have received the widget in the first place. It needs no floor exemption." And §0C.17's `FLOOR_EXEMPT` predicate itself, whose capability clause admits only `i.capability === null`, `i.capability.space === 'CONTROL'`, or a C9 ref whose `resourceClass === 'LOCAL'`.
findings.consequence: The `remedy` half of the claim is false under the declared predicate and is contradicted in terms by §0C.18. Verified in process: exactly one C9_CAPABILITIES row has `resourceClass: 'LOCAL'` and it is `c9.no_action` — never a widget's own owner capability — so an L11 remedy `REFINE` fails FLOOR_EXEMPT's third clause. The claim is also false in its first conjunct: only L11's remedy is fixed at `priority: 0`; §3.9 R3.9.3's refusal remedies and §2.6.14 LIMITATION's `remedy_intents[]` carry no such requirement, so "both added roles are `priority: 0`" does not hold in general either. Two normative clauses of equal precedence, both in Section 0-C, that cannot both be satisfied. The safety conclusion happens to survive on a different ground — the union ranges over `i ∈ emitted`, so it adds no intent and waives no floor, and a remedy withheld at ladder step 1 simply never appears — but the stated justification for EC-18 is not the one that holds, and §0C.17-ter's own doctrine forbids resting a fence on an argument that does not.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The escape intent is `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT` (§0C.18). The `remedy` role is neither, and need not be: the union ranges over intents already in `emitted`, so it adds no intent, waives no floor and confers nothing — a remedy withheld at §4.5.4 step 1 does not enter `reading_order` at all."

findings.clause: §3.1 `WidgetIntent`: "authority_hint: AuthorityHint;              // RENDERING HINT ONLY. Never read by any\n                                              // server decision (§3.14, FR-3)."
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.11-bis states the rule this breaks: "A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares." `AuthorityHint` has exactly two occurrences in the assembled 6451-line artefact — this declaration and §2.3.3 K7's prose "the same treatment given to `AuthorityHint`" — and no shape, table or errata row declares it. §0.3 declared the three root members §§1–4 never declared and stated "Every other root member is declared in §1 or §4"; `authority_hint` is an intent member and falls outside that sweep. It appears in no errata table (0.16, 0B.9, 0C.13), no NORMATIVE-PENDING binding, §0.17's register, §0.18's residuals or §0C.12.
findings.consequence: `authority_hint` is a non-nullable member of every `WidgetIntent`, and `intents.map(stripIntentToken)` is an input to `body_hash` (§1.9 H1), so both the hash input and §1.1.1 E2's closed-shape validator — which must refuse "any key not declared in this contract, at any depth" — are undefined over it; as specified, the only value `widgetEnvelope()` can admit is the empty object, which makes the field useless rather than dangerous. The consequence is contained and is NOT a conferral: §0.15 FR-3, §3.1 R3.1.3 and §0B.18's Gate 6 all fix that no server decision reads it, R3.1.3 names a CI reference test, and §0.54's forbidden-key walk is "a total walk over the serialized value", so a `role`, `permissions`, `is_staff` or `is_owner` key nested inside it would be refused at EP-MINT and EP-INGRESS. Filed because it meets the structural definition exactly and because the contract has adopted the rule against it; reported with its low consequence stated rather than inflated.
findings.fix: Either declare `AuthorityHint` in §3.1 with a closed member set carrying no authority vocabulary — for example `{ emphasis: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'muted'; disabled_because: ReasonCode | null }` — or delete the member outright and let `enabled: Cell<boolean>` carry the whole hint, which §2 K18 already specifies as the disabled rendering (`enabled: { state: 'UNAVAILABLE', reason_code: 'PERMISSION' }`). Deletion is the cleaner option: it removes a field FR-3 exists to disclaim.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18(3), line 2681: "At `EP-REGISTRY-LOAD` every `MOMENT_REGISTRY` row names a `moment_template_id` that resolves here, and every `required_cells` entry is a pointer the kind's leaf schema admits, or the process does not start."
findings.conflictsWith: EC-14's own declaration at §0C.28-bis line 2616: `interface Moment { moment_key: string; notify_pref_key: string; once_per: string; quiet_hours_policy: string; }` — `Moment` declares four members and none is `moment_template_id`. `MOMENT_REGISTRY` is `Readonly<Record<string, Moment>>` (line 2618), so a MOMENT_REGISTRY row is a `Moment`. The identifier occurs in only two other places in the whole contract: `MomentTemplate.moment_template_id` (line 2673 — the template's own id, not a pointer from a moment) and `ProactiveProvenance.moment_template_id` (line 6121 — a mint-time provenance field, not a registry row). This is the defect class §0C.11-bis states as a rule: "A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares."
findings.consequence: The named EP-REGISTRY-LOAD assertion cannot be written against the declared shapes. Read literally it evaluates `MOMENT_TEMPLATES[row.moment_template_id]` as `MOMENT_TEMPLATES[undefined]` for all twelve rows, so the assertion fails for every row and the process never starts — precisely the "fail-closed to the point of inertness, which is a defect and not a safety property" that EC-5 (§0C.20) rules against when it repairs its own first draft. It also leaves §4.9.4 PR5b with no declared route from a moment to the template whose `required_cells` drives the suppression branch, so the one mechanism PR5b names is unreachable from the moment the composer holds.
findings.fix: Add `moment_template_id: string;` to `interface Moment` in §0C.28-bis EC-14, and state that it MUST resolve in `MOMENT_TEMPLATES` at EP-REGISTRY-LOAD; or, if the moment→template edge is meant to live on the provenance, re-key EC-18(3)'s assertion on `ProactiveProvenance.moment_template_id` and say explicitly that MOMENT_REGISTRY rows carry no template pointer. Either edit is one line and closes PR5b's route at the same time.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18(2), line 2662: "**K22's derivation is amended** to `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { refKey({k:'intent', id}) : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`"
findings.conflictsWith: §4.8 declares `reading_order: InteractiveRef[]`, and `refKey` is declared at §0C.22-bis line 1995 as `declare function refKey(ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveRefKey;` — it maps a ref to a template-literal string key, never the reverse. Two same-precedence Section 0-C rules read reading_order as holding refs: §0C.22-bis line 2010, "`keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order.map(refKey))`", and §0C.22-ter's A-2 one-liner at line 2070, "`∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`". Separately, the set-builder's variable is unbound: the comprehension binds `i` and the element expression uses `id`.
findings.consequence: The escape and remedy entries enter `reading_order` as `InteractiveRefKey` strings while the rest are `InteractiveRef` objects, so the array violates its own declared element type and the two totality rules above apply `refKey`, `nameSourceOf` and `resolveInteractive` outside their declared domains for exactly those entries. As set equality the two clauses cannot both be satisfied: if reading_order holds refs, EC-18's derivation is wrong; if it holds keys, `reading_order.map(refKey)` and A-2's check are ill-typed. The concrete loss is that EC-6's accessible-name CI check — the one mechanism A-2 names — cannot be evaluated for the escape verb, which is the control §4.8 A-5 and §0B.36's CONSENT_STATE and PAYMENT_HANDOFF rows require to be always keyboard-reachable and named, and which EC-18(2) exists to make reachable.
findings.fix: Write the added term as refs, not keys, and bind the id to the comprehension variable: `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { {k:'intent', id: i.intent_ref} : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`. No other clause changes; §0C.22-bis's two totality rules then hold over the widened set unmodified.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18(2), line 2664, repeated verbatim in the §0C.13 errata row for EC-18 at line 2783: "Both added roles are `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT`, so this widens no authority — it makes an accessibility obligation the contract already states satisfiable."
findings.whyUnproven: FLOOR_EXEMPT is not a list; §0C.17 declares "Membership is DERIVED from declared members, never a list of names", so the predicate is the authority on what is in the set. Its third clause admits only `i.capability === null`, a `CONTROL` ref, or a `C9` ref whose `resourceClass === 'LOCAL'`. The role-'remedy' intent the contract actually mints is §4.1.3 L11's extension remedy, which §0C.18 declares "a `REFINE` on the widget's **own owner capability**" — a C9 key that is not the LOCAL row (verified by executing the registry: |{c ∈ C9_CAPABILITIES : resourceClass === 'LOCAL'}| = 1, and that row is c9.no_action, which is the no-action option's key, not a remedy's). The predicate therefore returns false for it. §0C.18 says so in terms — "**The L11 extension remedy is deliberately NOT in this set**, and the reason matters… It needs no floor exemption" — and §0C.32's EC-4 row fixes the membership at "Five intents satisfy it", a count EC-18's claim would break. The other role-'remedy' intents the contract mints, §2.6.14 `LIMITATION.remedy_intents`, are declared with no `priority` at all, so the `priority: 0` half is unsupported for them as well. The named mechanism does not classify these intents the way the sentence says it does, and no errata row and no NORMATIVE-PENDING marking covers the sentence: it is not prefixed [NON-NORMATIVE] and is not listed in §0C.12.
findings.fix: Replace the ground with the true one, which is stronger and needs no predicate: the comprehension ranges over `i ∈ emitted`, i.e. intents that have already passed `verificationFloor`, §4.5.4 steps 1–6 and the fitter, and `reading_order` is a presentation artefact that confers nothing — so no authority widens whether or not a remedy intent is FLOOR_EXEMPT. Delete the FLOOR_EXEMPT assertion from line 2664 and from the identical sentence in the §0C.13 EC-18 row, so that §0C.18's "deliberately NOT in this set" and §0C.32's count of five remain the single answer.

findings.clause: §0C.28-ter, the declaration of IntentRecord.c9_domain: "Mint class D, AUDIT_RETAINED. Non-null IFF BOTH capability.space === 'C9'. Derived at EP-MINT from `Correlation.agent_id` …"
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.28-quater, same section, same precedence: "On the run-less registered-capability-read path, `c9_domain` is `null` by construction, and EC-11's second Gate 6 `C9` branch reduces there to: the `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)]` row must exist …" — and §1.1.4, which declares `run_id` "NULLABLE BY DESIGN … because two paths mint envelopes", with §4.1.1 L1 naming the registered capability-read endpoint as minter 2 of 3.
findings.consequence: The word BOTH names a two-part condition and only one part is written; the missing conjunct is exactly the run-bearing scope -quater added. As written the IFF is unsatisfiable jointly with -quater: for a run-less capability-read envelope carrying a C9 intent the IFF demands a non-null `c9_domain` while -quater demands null, and the only declared derivation input (`Correlation.agent_id`) is null by construction on that path. An EP-MINT validator implementing the IFF literally must either refuse the envelope or write a value it cannot derive — reproducing, one line over, the precise outcome -quater exists to prevent ("The refusal as written would have made every C9 capability-read envelope unmintable"). The same condition is additionally keyed on `record.capability`, which §3.2's effect table fixes null for every HANDOFF, so every C9-subject HANDOFF also takes `c9_domain: null` while §0C.28-quinquies routes it into the branch that needs the value.
findings.fix: Restore the dropped conjunct and key it on the subject, not on `capability`: "Non-null IFF BOTH `subjectCapability(record).space === 'C9'` AND `correlation.run_id !== null`." That makes the IFF, -quater's null-by-construction ruling and -quinquies' dispatch key mutually consistent with no other edit.

findings.clause: §0C.28-bis EC-11's Gate 6 dispatch block: "else → WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)] must exist (else refuse), AND c9Capability(record.capability.key, record.c9_domain, C9_REGISTRY_HASH) must admit"
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.28-quinquies: "Gate 6 dispatches on `subjectCapability(record)`, not on `record.capability`. … The dispatch key is `subjectCapability(record).space` and the argument is `subjectCapability(record).key`" — together with §3.2's effect table, which fixes `capability` null for every `HANDOFF`.
findings.consequence: Round 10's repair was applied to the dispatch line and its comment ("// NOT record.capability — see below") but not to the call site two lines below, so the repair is inert for exactly the effect class it was written for. `subjectCapability` routes a HANDOFF into the C9 branch via `handoff_capability_ref`; the branch then evaluates `record.capability.key` on a member the contract fixes null, so the clause names `.key` on null. Gate 6 is a refusal point, so this fails closed — but it makes the branch unsatisfiable for every C9-subject HANDOFF whose key is one of the nine non-catalogue extras, including the `a22.configuration` handoff that §0C.11(5) names as newly reachable and that §0C.32's EC-2 row counts among the reductions it is compensating for. Two clauses of equal precedence cannot both be honoured: one passes `record.capability.key`, the other passes `subjectCapability(record).key`, and for a HANDOFF these differ and the first is null.
findings.fix: Rewrite the block's two remaining references to the subject: bind `ref = subjectCapability(record)` at the top of the branch, then `def = MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME.get(ref.key)` and `c9Capability(ref.key, record.c9_domain, C9_REGISTRY_HASH)`, with `record.c9_domain` itself derived per the corrected S1 condition.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18 item 2: "**K22's derivation is amended** to `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths(body)) ∪ { refKey({k:'intent', id}) : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`, with the escape placed **last** in render order."
findings.conflictsWith: §4.8, which declares `reading_order: InteractiveRef[]` and which §0C.22-bis preserves verbatim ("…role_hint, label, description, reading_order, live_region — unchanged…"); §0C.22-bis's own validator rule `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order.map(refKey))`; §0C.22's A-2 rule `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`; §2.2, where `interactive_paths: readonly string[]` is a field of `KindRule`, not a function; and §0C.11-bis's own rule that "a normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares", applied by §0C.22-ter to `intentOf` on the ground that it "occurred exactly once in the contract, inside the mechanism that used it".
findings.consequence: Four type-level defects in one normative derivation. (i) `refKey(...)` returns `InteractiveRefKey`, a template-literal string, and the amendment places it into an `InteractiveRef[]`; every other site maps the other way (`reading_order.map(refKey)`, `accessible_names[refKey(ref)]`), so K22's recompute-and-compare — "validateEnvelope recomputes the ref set from interactive_paths and refuses on any difference" — compares a set of objects against a set containing strings and can never match. Under the strict reading every input-locked envelope is refused at EP-MINT, which is the opposite of what EC-18 exists to achieve ("it makes an accessibility obligation the contract already states satisfiable"). (ii) `refs` is declared by no shape and occurs exactly once, in the mechanism that uses it — the same defect §0C.22-ter filed and repaired by declaring `resolveInteractive`. (iii) `interactive_paths(body)` applies a `readonly string[]` field as a function and omits its `KIND_REGISTRY[kind]` qualification. (iv) the set-builder binds `i` and then uses the free variable `id`.
findings.fix: `reading_order = refSet(KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths, body) ∪ { {k:'intent', id: i.intent_ref} : i ∈ emitted ∧ i.role ∈ {'escape','remedy'} }`, with `declare function refSet(paths: readonly string[], body: WidgetBody): InteractiveRef[]` declared once beside `resolveInteractive` under §0C.11-bis's rule. `i.intent_ref` is the right handle by §0.28 ("§4.8's `InteractiveRef` member `{ k: 'intent'; id }` holds an `intent_ref`").

findings.clause: §0C.13 row EC-17: "`InteractiveRef`'s **seven** members are the typed authority … K22's rule and mechanism stand verbatim", and its paragraph in §0C.10-bis: "per-kind membership is exactly what `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths` produces — which is what K22's *mechanism* already says … K22's rule survives verbatim; only its illustrative list is struck"
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.28-sexies EC-18 item 2 and §0C.13 row EC-18: "K22's derivation adds the `escape` and `remedy` intents, which every accessibility clause requires in `reading_order` and no kind lists" — both rows of the same errata table, same section, same precedence, neither marking the other VOID.
findings.consequence: EC-17 rules that per-kind membership of `reading_order` is *exactly* what `interactive_paths` produces; EC-18 rules that it is that set unioned with the emitted escape and remedy intents, which by EC-18's own admission "no kind lists". The two cannot both be satisfied: under EC-17 an envelope whose `reading_order` carries the escape ref is refused at EP-MINT as an extra ref, and under EC-18 an envelope without it is refused as a missing one. Every envelope with `lifecycle.input_lock !== 'none'` — i.e. every envelope §0.25 mandates an escape on — sits in the intersection. This is the staleness EC-17 itself condemns ("a list that drifts from the type it illustrates becomes a second, wrong answer") turned on EC-17's own ruling, and §0C.1's round-10 note ("five stale cross-references this section had left behind") shows the sweep missed this one.
findings.fix: Amend EC-17's row and paragraph to read "K22's rule and mechanism stand verbatim **as amended by EC-18**", and restate its membership sentence as "per-kind membership is exactly what `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths` produces, plus the emitted `escape` and `remedy` intents (EC-18)".

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18 item 3: "At `EP-REGISTRY-LOAD` every `MOMENT_REGISTRY` row names a `moment_template_id` that resolves here, and every `required_cells` entry is a pointer the kind's leaf schema admits, or the process does not start."
findings.conflictsWith: §0C.28-bis EC-14, which declares the only shape a `MOMENT_REGISTRY` row has: `interface Moment { moment_key: string; notify_pref_key: string; once_per: string; quiet_hours_policy: string; }` — four members, none of them `moment_template_id` and none of them a `WidgetKind`.
findings.consequence: A normative EP-REGISTRY-LOAD assertion reads two things off a row that declares neither: `moment_template_id` (the only declared `moment_template_id` in the contract is on `ProactiveProvenance`, §4.9.3, which is a per-emission member and not a registry row) and "the kind's leaf schema" (neither `Moment` nor `MomentTemplate` names a `WidgetKind`, so the phrase has no referent and the pointer check has no schema to check against). The assertion set can never pass, which by §A2.4's own discipline means the process does not start — so EC-18's declaration of `MomentTemplate`, the repair that makes §4.9.4 PR5b's `required_cells` suppression constructible, is inoperative. This is the same defect class EC-6 exists to close (a CI check over an identifier no shape declares), reproduced in its own repair.
findings.fix: Add the two members the assertion reads: `interface Moment { moment_key: string; kind: WidgetKind; moment_template_id: string; notify_pref_key: string; once_per: string; quiet_hours_policy: string; }`, and state the pointer check as "every `required_cells` entry is a pointer `KIND_REGISTRY[row.kind]`'s leaf schema admits".

findings.conflictsWith: §A1.2's P-13 row, whose component is "**CHART read facade** — a widget-layer read facade returning `rows_digest` and `series_digest`" and whose "Depends on it" column lists only FR-10, §2.6.9 CHART.1 and `ChartBody.rows_digest`/`.series_digest`; §0C.29's P-32 row, which enumerates EC-14's dependents as "§4.9.3 PR3c; §4.9.2 PR2 (b); the twelve-row totality of `MOMENT_REGISTRY`" and names no CHART component; and §0C.20's assertion: "a clause bound to no row, or a clause whose status names a `p_ref` whose row does not list it, fails the assertion and the process does not start."
findings.consequence: EC-14 is the delivery-consent repair — `notify_pref_key`, `MOMENT_REGISTRY`, `NOTIFICATION_CONSENT_REGISTRY`. It is bound to the CHART read facade, a wave-4 K10 component that gates nothing EC-14 names. Two live consequences: §0C.20's EP-REGISTRY-LOAD assertion fails on its own stated terms, because P-13's row does not list EC-14; and, if the ledger is instead populated from status lines, §A2.1 then holds PR3c's guarded capability at `capability_gap_ref` with no actuating control, and §A2.7 forbids discharging it, until the CHART digest facade ships — a prerequisite chain no row records and no reader could reconstruct. §0C.29's P-32 row is K13/wave 5; P-13 is K10/wave 4; the two are unrelated deliverables. This is the sixth stale cross-reference of the five §0C.1 says round 10 closed.
findings.fix: Replace P-13 with **P-17** — `control.delivery.resolve`, "the handler that resolves one `dedupe_key` across channels" (§A1.3, K13/wave 5), which is the component PR3c's own third condition ("`dedupe_key` must be unique for the moment's `once_per` window") actually needs — or drop the second binding and leave EC-14 pending on P-32 alone.

findings.clause: §0C.28-sexies EC-18 item 2: "Both added roles are `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT`, so this widens no authority — it makes an accessibility obligation the contract already states satisfiable." Restated in §0C.13's EC-18 row: "both are `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT`, so no authority widens."
findings.whyUnproven: `FLOOR_EXEMPT` is a derived predicate (§0C.17), and it is false for `role: 'remedy'` on both conjuncts. Its capability clause admits only `i.capability === null`, a `CONTROL` ref, or a C9 ref whose `resourceClass === 'LOCAL'` — and the section's own build veto asserts that set has cardinality one (`|{c ∈ C9_CAPABILITIES : c.resourceClass === 'LOCAL'}| === 1`, which I confirmed by enumeration: the single row is `c9.no_action`). §4.1.3 L11's remedy intent is "a `REFINE` on the widget's **own owner capability**", never `c9.no_action`, so the clause excludes it. §0C.18 says so in terms: "**The L11 extension remedy is deliberately NOT in this set**, and the reason matters … It needs no floor exemption, and it keeps the protection it already had." The priority conjunct also fails in general: `role: 'remedy'` is not confined to L11 — §2.6.14's `remedy_intents[]` on a `LIMITATION` body and §3.9.3's refusal remedies carry the role at no declared priority, and `LIMITATION`'s permitted effects (NONE, NAVIGATE, HANDOFF, plus §0.21's CONTROL) put a NAVIGATE remedy outside the effect clause as well. No errata row, no NORMATIVE-PENDING marking and no §0C.12 listing covers the sentence, and §0C.18's own audit table enumerates the exempt set at five with an explicit note that "a reader who expects six and counts five should find the answer here". Nothing is conferred by the error — `reading_order` is an accessibility ordering that gates no authority, and the floor a remedy intent actually carries is unchanged — so this is a false justification, not a security hole. It matters because it is the only argument EC-18 offers for the widening, and a reader who implements the sentence rather than the predicate would add `'remedy'` to the exempt set and thereby zero EFFECT_FLOOR, KIND_FLOOR and targetFloor on a REFINE that carries the widget's own owner capability.
findings.fix: Replace the justification with the true one: "The escape intent is `priority: 0` and `FLOOR_EXEMPT` (§0C.17); a `remedy` intent is neither, and needs neither — `reading_order` is an accessibility ordering and gates no authority, so its membership widens nothing. A withheld remedy simply does not appear, because the union is taken over `emitted`."

findings.clause: §0C.32's floor-reduction table, EC-2 row: "What still fences these nine: their `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row, `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR`, and — new in EC-11 — Gate 6's second C9 branch, `c9Capability`'s own admission."
findings.whyUnproven: §0C.28-quater, in the same section, rules that mechanism out on the path that carries five of the nine: "On the run-less registered-capability-read path, `c9_domain` is `null` by construction, and EC-11's second Gate 6 `C9` branch **reduces there to**: the `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)]` row must exist (else refuse), plus `c9Floor`'s `min_verification` and `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR` carried at Gate 5. **The `c9Capability` domain half is explicitly NOT applied on that path**." The run-less registered-capability-read endpoint is minter 2 of 3 (§4.1.1 L1) and is precisely how the five `SOURCE_READ` keys of the nine are read — `c7.measurement.read`, `c8.result.read`, `b35.status`, `owner_report.status`, `owner_report.download` — which are also the five whose floor EC-2 reduces not to a fixed level but to "whatever their own `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row and consent class require". So for exactly the keys with the least residual protection, the compensating fence the audit table names does not run, and the residual reduces to the row-existence check plus a verification *level*, which is not a role test: §0C.28-bis itself concedes that `c9Capability` "applies no role, surface, feature or risk-tier test, which `assertCanExecute` does" and warns that "a reader must not take this branch for an equivalent of the first". The claim is therefore a normative sentence naming a mechanism that does not do what the sentence says on the governing path, and it is not covered by a NORMATIVE-PENDING marking — the defect is not that the branch is unbuilt (it is, on P-01/P-26/P-30) but that as specified it never applies there. This matters because §0C.32 declares itself the single audit surface for every floor this section lowers ("A reader auditing this contract should be able to find every floor reduction it makes by reading this table"), so an over-stated compensating fence defeats the table's purpose. It is not a security-contract violation: all nine are C9-space read/propose keys that only `REFINE`/`DRAFT`/`HANDOFF`/class-`c` `NAVIGATE` may carry (§0B.7), none can actuate, `min_verification: SESSION_VERIFIED` still excludes every client principal (§1.7 K1 makes SESSION_VERIFIED require an active Membership), and §0.17 item 2's normative remainder keeps the projector on the same service call sites the non-widget read paths use, so the underlying read owner's own authorisation still applies.
findings.fix: Scope the row to the path: "…and — new in EC-11 — Gate 6's second C9 branch, `c9Capability`'s own admission, **on the run-bearing path only** (`b35.preview`, `b35.confirm`, `a22.configuration`, `c9.no_action`). On the run-less registered-capability-read path §0C.28-quater withdraws that admission, so the residual fence for `c7.measurement.read`, `c8.result.read`, `b35.status`, `owner_report.status` and `owner_report.download` is their policy row's `min_verification` and `consent_class` at Gate 5, plus the read owner's own authorisation at its call site (§0.17 item 2) — and no role test at Gate 6." Alternatively, require a role fence for those five by giving §0C.20's P-10 row a normative `min_verification` floor for the owner-report keys.
